summary: Module 4 CONTEXT micro-exercise. (1) Before reading any code for a 3-second API: (a) measure the request's time distribution -- start/end timestamps in structured logs to see WHERE the 3s lives (network, app, DB, Redis); (b) run a profiler against a live or replayed request (cProfile/py-spy for CPU, tracemalloc/heapy for memory) and check pg_stat_statements / EXPLAIN ANALYZE for slow queries. The flashlight-before-blueprints move: observe the running system first. (2) CPU profiler shows where execution time is spent; memory profiler shows where memory is allocated and whether it is released. For a service getting slower over hours, I would run a MEMORY profiler first -- gradual degradation over hours points at a connection/listener/cache leak (the restaurant that never clears tables), not a CPU hotspot; a leak exhausts the pool and every subsequent request stalls, which reads as 'slow over time' even though the CPU profile looks fine.
